doc.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: LaFaro's influence on Flanigan's playing
summary: He discovered LaFaro through Hawes, Coleman and Evans records and was struck by their shared hometown.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well he was quite a pioneer of a sorts on the bass, and his work, did it affect your own playing?

Well yeah. I mean I discovered his playing through Hampton Hawes records and Ornette Coleman records and of course the Bill Evans stuff, not to mention a bunch of others. But I thought, wow, that’s a different approach and I really like that. And then I found out my close connection with him, and I was sort of shocked. I mean here I am going to high school, trying to learn how to wail on the bass, and then finding out that this pioneer cat, I’m walking the same hallowed halls and this kind of thing. I used to visit his grave all the time, yeah. I probably saw him, I probably laid eyes on him, but he died when I was five, so I don’t recall. It’s possible.
Plus he probably wasn’t carrying a bass down the street.
No, he was probably just hanging out.
